topics.name: Greetings

words.tip: 多謝 (do1 ze6) is for gifts & compliments. For a service (someone holds the door), say 唔該 (m4 goi1).
唔該 (m4 goi1) is super useful: please, excuse me, AND thanks for a service.

words.r: hou2 gou1 hing3 jing6 sik1 nei5

topics.note: 唔該 (m4 goi1) = please / thanks for a service; 多謝 (do1 ze6) = thanks for a gift. 早唞 is a casual “good night”; 午安 is formal, most people just say 你好.

topics.name: Numbers

words.tip: 四 (sei3) sounds like 死 (sei2, death), so 4 is unlucky.
八 (baat3) rhymes with 發 (faat3, prosper): lucky! 🍀

sentences.r: m4 goi1 jat1 bui1 gaa3 fe1
ngo5 jau5 loeng5 go3 hing1 dai6

topics.note: Jyutping numbers 1–6 are tones: 1 high, 2 rising, 3 mid, 4 low falling, 5 low rising, 6 low.

words.tip: 芝士 (zi1 si2) comes from the English word “cheese” 🧀.
啡色 (fe1 sik1) = coffee, 咖啡 (gaa3 fe1), color ☕.

words.tip: 細佬 (sai3 lou2) literally means “little guy”.

topics.note: 嫲嫲/爺爺 are your dad's parents; mom's parents are 婆婆/公公 (po4 po2 / gung4 gung1).

words.tip: 係 (hai6) = “is / yes”. Add 唔 (m4) for “not”: 唔係 (m4 hai6) = no.

topics.name: Grammar: Past tense

sentences.en: I went to the park yesterday.
sentences.r: ngo5 kam4 jat6 heoi3 zo2 gung1 jyun2
ngo5 kam4 maan5 sik6 zo2 laai1 min6

sentences.en: I saw a movie last week.
sentences.r: ngo5 soeng6 go3 sing1 kei4 tai2 zo2 tou3 hei3
ngo5 ji5 ging1 zou6 jyun4 gung1 fo3

topics.note: Cantonese verbs don't change. Add 咗 (zo2) after the verb for a finished action: 我食咗 (ngo5 sik6 zo2) = I ate. Time words like 琴日 (kam4 jat6) go before the verb.

topics.name: Grammar: Future

sentences.en: I will go to the beach tomorrow.
sentences.r: ngo5 ting1 jat6 wui5 heoi3 hoi2 taan1
ngo5 gam1 maan5 jiu3 wan1 syu1

sentences.en: Next year I will travel a lot.
sentences.t: 出年我會去好多地方旅行。
sentences.r: ceot1 nin2 ngo5 wui5 heoi3 hou2 do1 dei6 fong1 leoi5 hang4
ngo5 dang2 zan6 daa2 bei2 nei5

sentences.en: My dream is to be a singer.
sentences.r: ngo5 ge3 mung6 soeng2 hai6 zou6 go1 sau2

topics.note: Use 會 (wui5) = will, or 要 (jiu3) = going to: 我會去 (ngo5 wui5 heoi3) = I will go. Time words like 聽日 (ting1 jat6) make the future clear.

topics.name: Grammar: Questions

words.r: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5

sentences.r: go2 go3 jan4 hai6 bin1 go3

topics.note: Yes/no questions often use verb + 唔 (m4) + verb: 啱唔啱？(ngaam1 m4 ngaam1?) = right or not? Question words: 咩 (me1) what, 邊度 (bin1 dou6) where.

topics.name: Grammar: Negation

sentences.r: ngo5 gam1 jat6 mou5 si4 gaan3
ne1 go3 m4 hai6 ngo5 go3 doi2

topics.note: 唔 (m4) = don't / not. 冇 (mou5) = don't have / didn't. 未 (mei6) = not yet: 我仲未食 (ngo5 zung6 mei6 sik6) = I haven't eaten yet.

topics.name: Grammar: Polite vs casual

sentences.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom? (polite)
sentences.r: cing2 man6 sai2 sau2 gaan1 hai2 bin1 dou6
deoi3 m4 zyu6 ngo5 ci4 dou3 zo2
m4 hou2 ji3 si1 ngo5 ge3 co3

topics.note: Cantonese shows politeness with words like 請問 (cing2 man6) and 唔該 (m4 goi1) more than a special 'you'. 晒 (saai3) adds extra thanks: 多謝晒 (do1 ze6 saai3).
